subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron tool restriction be a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` config surface, explicit inheritance from `tools.subagents.tools`, or part of a broader per-session policy design such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49183?
rationale: This adds security-sensitive public config/default behavior, and the wrong precedence could either leave the gap open or break existing cron jobs that rely on message/tool access.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Implement `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against global policy, per-job `payload.toolsAllow`, delivery modes, and CLI-backed runtimes.

options.title: Reuse subagent policy
options.body: Make cron sessions explicitly inherit `tools.subagents.tools` only if maintainers accept the semantic coupling and document it as a shared delegated-session policy.

options.title: Fold into broader session policy
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer implementation until the broader per-session policy RFC defines one policy model for cron, spawned, sender, and scope-based sessions.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Implement `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against global policy, per-job `payload.toolsAllow`, delivery modes, and CLI-backed runtimes.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and prior review history place Peter closest to the config/tool-resolution decision surface.
